runs.failure_point: Its scans never showed the investigation matter, the settlement matter that surfaced in path searches was never opened, and it wrote six other matters.

first_error.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
first_error.why: The store-wide scan was printed only as the first lines of each range and the first 100 file headers, so the investigation matter never appeared, and the later stricter scan ran only over matters from the file-name list, which did not include it.
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) The review at [91] said the scan's matter set came from the earlier file-name list, so matters outside it were never scanned; the agent went to writing.

other_errors.why: The settlement matter appeared in the agent's path search at [18] and [26], but the listing at [45] covered sixteen other matters and it was never listed or read, although it surfaced again at [54] and [85].
other_errors.critic_note: (generic flag) Reviews at [48], [56] and [81] said surfaced matters were left unopened; the one at [56] named the matter's number series only.

other_errors.why: The answer asserts six matters, documented in drafts, term sheets and transaction diligence memos, as qualifying (evidence seen at [59]-[71], [85]-[89]).
other_errors.critic_note: (specific flag) The screening review at [73] said two matters rested only on drafts and the write review warned of an inflated count; the check stage softened one row but kept all six.

divergence: All fail, in different ways, and all three wrote executive-employment negotiations known only from drafts and term sheets as qualifying (over-inclusion). T0: both needed matters surfaced in its scan tally, but the screening stage read file-name picks and neither was opened (surfaced-not-opened at screening); a later review named one of them and was ignored. T1 is the only run that opened both: it listed and read them, wrote the settlement matter, but excluded the investigation matter because its acceleration was later forfeited (under-inclusion at the write stage, not flagged), and the critic's specific draft-only flag led only to a headline split. T2: its scans were printed in capped heads and a later scan was restricted to the file-name list, so one matter never appeared (search-miss), and the other, which surfaced in path searches, was never listed (surfaced-not-opened). The split between T1 and the others is at the listing/screening choice after the scans: T1 listed matters named in its scan snippets, T0 and T2 chose from file names.
